stem: The length of a rectangle is twice its breadth, and its area is $128\ \text{cm}^2$. Let the breadth be $b$ cm. Mark on the number line every value of $b$ that is possible for this rectangle.
solution: Let the breadth be $b$ cm, so the length is $2b$ cm.
Area = length $\times$ breadth, so $2b \times b = 128$, which is $2b^2 = 128$.
Bring every term to one side and divide both sides by $2$: $b^2 - 64 = 0$.
Factorise as a difference of squares: $(b - 8)(b + 8) = 0$.
A product is zero only when a factor is zero, so $b = 8$ or $b = -8$.

Check each solution against the story. The breadth is a length, and a length cannot be negative, so $b = -8$ is ruled out. $b = 8$ gives a length of $16$ cm and an area of $8 \times 16 = 128\ \text{cm}^2$, which fits.
Mark only $8$ on the number line.
notes: The contrast partner of keep-every-solution-that-fits: here the negative root is ruled out by the context (a breadth is a length), so a student who has absorbed "keep both solutions" from the first template is refuted by extra-values on -8. A student who has the opposite reflex (always drop the negative) gets this one right, which is why the pair must be served together. Only extra-values is mapped. sign-flipped (marking only -8) is also the misconception's "or the wrong one" reading, but it needs a student to choose the negative root alone and is rare, so it is left unmapped rather than listing the same misconception twice. missed-values (8 not marked) comes from a bad solve and diagnoses nothing specific. The widget asks for the breadth only so the target stays inside the instrument's range (the length 16 would not fit in a 24-wide range centred on 0 with room for the negative root). Limits: range [-10,10] is 20 wide and within +-20; the single target 8 is a whole number inside it, and -8 is inside it so the error can be made.
